## 1. Chart type
- **Flow map / migration chord-style map** over a world map.
- It shows **directed flows** between regions using curved arrows, plus **self-loops** for within-continent migration.

## 2. Layout techniques
- **Geographic layout**: regions are positioned on a world map.
- **Flow links**: curved arrows connect origin and destination regions.
- **Variable-width links**: arrow thickness appears to encode migration volume.
- **Self-loop circles**: large circular arrows around regions indicate migration within the same continent.
- No faceting or small multiples.

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Continent / Region (e.g., North America, Latin America, Europe, Asia, Africa, Oceania) | Categorical/nominal | Geographic position on map; text labels |
| Migration flow volume (in millions) | Quantitative | Arrow/flow thickness; numeric labels on flows and loops |
| Origin region | Categorical/nominal | Start point of curved arrow on map |
| Destination region | Categorical/nominal | End point / arrowhead location on map |
| Within-continent migration | Categorical/nominal relationship | Circular self-loop arrows around each region |
| Year (2017) | Temporal | Title text (“Migration in 2017”) |

## 1. Chart type
- **Flow map / migration chord-style map** over a world map.
- It shows **directed flows** between regions using curved arrows, plus **self-loops** for within-continent migration.

## 2. Layout techniques
- **Geographic layout**: regions are positioned on a world map.
- **Flow links**: curved arrows connect origin and destination regions.
- **Variable-width links**: arrow thickness appears to encode migration volume.
- **Self-loop circles**: large circular arrows around regions indicate migration within the same continent.
- No faceting or small multiples.

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Continent / Region (e.g., North America, Latin America, Europe, Asia, Africa, Oceania) | Categorical/nominal | Geographic position on map; text labels |
| Migration flow volume (in millions) | Quantitative | Arrow/flow thickness; numeric labels on flows and loops |
| Origin region | Categorical/nominal | Start point of curved arrow on map |
| Destination region | Categorical/nominal | End point / arrowhead location on map |
| Within-continent migration | Categorical/nominal relationship | Circular self-loop arrows around each region |
| Year (2017) | Temporal | Title text (“Migration in 2017”) |
raw_comment:
Have you ever seen a map that is called a graph?  Here is one that makes showing migration within and between continents easy to comprehend.  You wondered about several aspects of the graph.  Was this the migration of people or animals?  Did people migrate only in one direction in their continent?  Why were there no numbers on the dashed lines?  What’s going on in Asia?

You had many catchy headlines including Katie of Eden Prairie, MN whose headline had a double entendre "Migration in Millions: How the World Moves".  Good noticing and wondering leads to snappy headlines.

Thanks to all teachers and students who responded.  You can continue to post responses. Talk to your classmates and read the moderators’ replies. Dig deeper into what the graph shows. Signing off -- Sharon in Boston, where 27% of the population is foreign-born, and Corey Andreasen in Qatar, where 88% of the population is foreign-born. Visit the "What's Going On In This Graph?" archives to keep responding. Hope to see you next week.
